beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Exporting files does not reproduce the whole working setup.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Continuity means that the worker and accepted work remain usable through those changes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This design suggests a catalog of capabilities with explicit outcomes and requirements.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Each entry needs permissions, supported environments, and evaluated versions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed sequence begins with useful workflows and repeatable deployment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Broader distribution depends on capabilities that people can maintain.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Integration, administration, and support are possible services, not established commercial results.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Security, maintenance, deployment complexity, and existing competitors remain practical risks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A large package count alone would not resolve them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The supplier comparison offers a bounded pilot with a recognizable output.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An experienced reviewer can check its sources and identify costly omissions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Measure human effort across preparation, intervention, review, and repair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Include setup, execution, maintenance, and failed assignments in the total cost.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The pilot succeeds when those costs improve while required conditions remain intact.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Human clarification can remain part of a useful workflow.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: If repair consumes the saving, investigate the specific tool, procedure, or workflow failure.
